title: Expansion microscopy of the chick embryo neural tube to overcome molecular crowding at the centrosomes-cilia
protocol: Remove the eggs from the incubator.
Cut around the vascular area using long and thin tip scissors.
Remove the embryo from the egg using forceps or a small spoon.
Place embryos in 1× PBS in a Petri dish.
Remove extraembryonic membranes by gently scraping using fine forceps.
Replace 1× PBS with ice cold methanol and incubate for 16 hours at -20°C.
Pour off cold methanol and replace it with 1× PBS.
Prepare agarose/saccharose solution (0.5% low-melt agarose, 1% saccharose in H2O) and keep it molten in a warm bath.
Remove head and heart by gently scraping with fine forceps if performing NT transversal sections.
Cut through the NT at the level of the wing bud caudal to the limb bud with fine forceps.
Transfer the embryo trunk into the plastic sectioning mold.
Place molten agarose/saccharose solution into the plastic sectioning mold.
Avoid embedding the tissue in overheated agarose/saccharose solution.
Use fine forceps to lift and orient all NTs in parallel and flat on their ventral side in the agarose.
Once the agarose is hardened, use a flat surface tool to remove the agarose block from the mold.
Carve with a razor blade to remove excess agarose and orient it for desired transversal section plane.
Add a drop of super glue to the vibratome stage, place the agarose block on it, and fill the vibratome stage with water.
Set the parameters of the vibratome to speed-6; frequency: 65 Hz (if applicable); thickness-50 μm and section.
With a thin paint brush, collect sections carefully trying not to break tissue slices and place into a 1× PBS-filled 24 multiwell plate.
Stabilize the embryo on a petri dish coated with PDMS by pinning at the level of the wing and the limb buds from both sides of the neural tube (NT).
Gently stretch the pinned embryo to ensure visibility of the NT and somites.
Use a tungsten needle to gently scrape and open the dorsal part of the NT.
Scrape longitudinally along the dorsal NT in a caudo-rostral direction.
Separate the somites from the NT using a tungsten needle by scraping longitudinally on each side of the NT.
Cut the NT at the level of the wing bud and caudal to the limb bud.
Lift the whole NT out of the embryo in one smooth rostral to caudal motion using forceps.
Transfer the open-book NT to a 200 μL PCR tube containing 1× PBS with a glass pipette.
Incubate tissue slices in permeabilization buffer (0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 10 min on an orbital shaker at low speed at 20°C.
Incubate tissue slices in the saturation buffer (1% BSA/0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 30 min on an orbital shaker at 20°C.
Incubate tissue slices with primary antibodies diluted in the blocking solution (1% BSA/0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 16 h on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Wash tissue slices three times in the permeabilization buffer (0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 15 min each wash.
Incubate tissue slices with secondary antibodies diluted at 1:500 in the blocking solution (1% BSA/0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 2 h on an orbital shaker at 20°C.
Wash tissue slices three times with the permeabilization buffer (0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 15 min each wash.
Incubate open-book NT in permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 2 h on a rotary shaker at 20°C.
Incubate open-book NT in saturation buffer (1% BSA/0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 16 hours on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Wash open-book NT three times with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS), each wash lasting 15 minutes.
Incubate open-book NT with primary antibodies diluted in the blocking solution (1% BSA/0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 16 hours on a rotary shaker at 4°C.
Wash open-book NT three times with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS), each wash lasting 15 minutes.
Incubate open-book NT with secondary antibodies in the blocking solution (1% BSA/0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS) for 16 hours on an orbital shaker at 4°C.
Wash open-book NT three times with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS), each wash lasting 15 minutes.
Prepare the gelation chamber using a suitable large container with a lid.
Cover the external part of the container with aluminum foil.
Cover the internal bottom of the container with parafilm.
Place a round coverslip of 13 mm diameter on top of the parafilm.
Add 60 μL of 1× PBS onto the coverslip.
Apply tissue paper soaked in sterile water along the circular periphery of the chamber to maintain humidity.
Isolate tissue slices using tungsten needles under a dissection microscope.
Soak tungsten needles and spoons in horse serum before dissection.
Gently isolate H2B-RFP electroporated side using fine forceps under a fluorescent dissecting microscope.
Transfer the tissue to 60 μL of 1× PBS on top of the coverslip in the gelation chamber using spoon micro-spatula or handmade spoon glass micropipette.
Prepare anchoring solution by diluting anchoring Reagent Stock (10 mg/mL Acryloyl-X in anhydrous DMSO) to 0.1 mg/mL in 1× PBS pH7.4.
Remove the 1× PBS from the coverslip with a 10 μL pipette.
Add 60 μL of anchoring solution onto the tissue on the coverslip.
Place the lid on the humidified chamber and leave the tissue in AcX solution for 16 hours in the dark at 20°C.
Thaw components for the gelling solution on ice.
Remove Acryloyl-X from the coverslip.
Wash tissues with 60 μL of 1× PBS twice, each time for 15 minutes.
Reposition tissues in the center and close to the coverslip using a tungsten needle during the last wash.
Drain excess 1× PBS from the tissues.
Prepare 60 μL of gelling buffer by adding monomer solution first.
Add 4HT to the gelling buffer.
Add TEMED to the gelling buffer.
Lastly, add APS in a 47:1:1:1 ratio to the gelling buffer.
Vortex the gelling buffer for a few seconds.
Keep the mixed gelling solution on ice to prevent premature gelation.
Place a 60 μL drop of gelation buffer on parafilm.
Carefully flip over the coverslip where tissues are attached onto the drop of gelation buffer.
Incubate tissues for 2-2.5 h at 37°C.
Prepare the digestion buffer with a final concentration of Proteinase K at 8 U/mL.
Insert flat tweezers from the side between the parafilm and the gels and gently flip the gel that remains attached to the coverslip.
Transfer the gel and the attached coverslip to a 35 mm diameter well plate.
Add 3 mL of digestion buffer for each 60-70 μL gel.
Leave the gel immersed in the digestion buffer for 4-4.5 h at 37°C in the dark.
After digestion, detach the gel from the coverslip.
Expand the gel 1.5×.
Wash the gel three times with 1× PBS for 10 minutes each to remove excess proteinase K.
Add DAPI at a 1:1000 dilution in 1× PBS to the gel and incubate for 16 hours at 4°C.
If later expansion is desired, remove digestion buffer, add enough 1× PBS to avoid dehydration, and store the gel at 4°C in the dark for up to one week.
Transfer the gel to a 100 mm petri dish by inversion.
Remove the 1× PBS from the gel using a 15 mL pipette.
Immerse the gel in milliQ-H2O for 20 minutes at 20°C.
Repeat the milliQ-H2O washes two more times.
The sample should be fully expanded and optically cleared prior to imaging.
Wash the gel three times for 20 minutes in petri dishes.
Continue washing the gel with milliQ-H2O until no further expansion is observed.
Locate the tissue inside the gel using UV light under a dissecting microscope.
Use a sharp scalpel blade to cut and select the gel containing the tissue.
Place the gel directly onto a polylysine-coated coverslip.
Remove excess water carefully from the coverslip with a paper tissue.
Transfer the gel onto the microscope stage.
Locate and image the whole NT using a 10× dry lens with a 0.3 NA.
Switch to a 63× oil-immersion lens for imaging centrosomes and cilia within the cells.
Determine a rectangular cropped region of interest to speed up imaging with optimal XY acquisition settings.
Acquire images with a 40 nm pixel size in Superresolution mode.
Capture Z-slices with a step size of 0.5 μm using piezoelectric stage.
Acquire images with frame-by-frame acquisition for up to 4 channels (405 nm, 488 nm, 561 nm and 633 nm).
Reconstruct Raw Fast Airyscan data automatically with Zen black software.
Use ImageJ to calculate the distances between local maxima from the intensity plot profiles on the expanded sample images.
